page: Microsoft Azure HB120-96rs_v3 is a high-performance computing instance within the HBv3 family, deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 processor architecture offering 96 dedicated vCPUs. To support memory-intensive compute tasks, the instance provides 456.0 GB of system memory, which yields an allocation of 4.75 GB of RAM per dedicated core. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs configured on this virtual machine.

For local high-throughput scratch data and caching, the instance features a bundled 2435 GB NVMe SSD. It also includes support for RDMA networking and Premium Storage integration. Networking does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires infrastructure routing or separate address provisioning for direct external egress.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the provision of 96 fully dedicated cores combined with 2435 GB of integrated high-speed NVMe storage reduces external I/O overhead. This configuration is aligned with compute and simulation demands where consistent per-core execution and fast local disk access are critical. Tradeoffs include the lack of bundled public IPv4 routing and the absence of hardware accelerators like GPUs.

Microsoft Azure HB120-96rs_v3 fits high-performance computing tasks including computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, weather simulation, molecular dynamics, distributed batch processing, and memory-aligned scientific computing workloads requiring RDMA fabrics.
